name: Doubled word

source.quote: Doubled and dropped words. "the the," "to to," or a missing a or the left behind by an edit.

message: The same word appears twice in a row, usually left behind by an edit.
fix: Delete one copy.

flag: Select the the project to open it.
pass: Select the project to open it.
The report shows that that setting is off.

name: Long sentence

source.quote: One idea per sentence. Short sentences translate better.

message: This sentence runs past 30 words. The guide sets no number, so 30 is this tool's threshold. Long sentences usually carry two ideas.
fix: Split it at the second idea, or cut words that don't carry a fact.

flag: To make sure that your whole team always sees the very latest numbers from every single connected source without needing to refresh the page manually, the dashboard refreshes itself automatically every five minutes.
pass: The dashboard refreshes every 5 minutes, so your team sees the latest numbers.

name: Long paragraph

source.quote: One topic per paragraph, stated in the first sentence.

message: This paragraph runs past 150 words. The guide sets no number, so 150 is this tool's threshold. A paragraph this long usually covers more than one topic.
fix: Split it where the topic changes, and state each topic in its first sentence.

flag: Word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word.

name: Passive voice

source.quote: In active voice, the subject does the action. Convert passive to active only when the actor is named or obvious.

message: A "was done by" sentence hides the actor at the end. The guide converts to active only when the actor is named or obvious, and keeps passive when it keeps blame off the reader or when the receiver is the point. Only passives with an explicit "by" are flagged.
fix: Put the actor first: "The scheduler generates the report every Monday."

flag: The report is generated by the scheduler every Monday.
pass: The scheduler generates the report every Monday.

name: Use present tense

source.quote: Opens, not will open. Present tense describes how the product behaves every time.

message: Product behavior that happens every time is described in the present tense. A real statement about timing ("will be available in the next release") is a fact and stays.
fix: Use the present tense: "the dialog closes".

flag: When you select Save, the dialog will close.
pass: When you select Save, the dialog closes.
The feature will be available in the next release.

name: Describe only what ships today

source.section: Writing about product behavior > Describe only what ships today
source.quote: Write about behavior that exists in the released product. Don't describe planned features, roadmap items, or capabilities behind a setting the reader can't turn on.

message: A feature guide that describes a planned feature becomes a promise. The guide moves such statements to release notes or a roadmap. This is a flag for the author, not an edit.
fix: Flag it: is this released? If not, move it to the release notes or the roadmap.

flag: Two-way calendar sync is coming soon.
Real-time export is coming in a future release.
pass: Export runs on a daily schedule.

name: Vague claim with a missing fact

source.section: Sentences > Flag vague claims, don't sharpen them
source.quote: A vague phrase usually hides a missing fact: an interval, a count, a limit, or a condition.

message: This phrase stands in for a specific value: an interval, a count, a limit, or a condition. If you're editing, you can't supply it.
fix: Flag it for the author. Rewrite only if the specific value appears elsewhere in the source.

flag: The dashboard updates in near real time.
The connector may not always work as expected.

name: Sentence that only announces

source.quote: "The table below shows the supported connectors." The table is right there. "This section explains how to configure notifications." The heading already said so.

message: A sentence that introduces the next thing adds length and no information. The heading or the table already says it.
fix: Cut it, unless it carries a fact the heading doesn't. Then move the fact and cut. If cutting it would leave a heading directly above another heading, rewrite it to state what the section covers instead.

flag: The table below shows the supported connectors.
This section explains how to configure notifications.

name: "It is important to note"

source.quote: "It is important to note that ..." State the thing.

message: The opener delays the point.
fix: State the thing.

flag: It is important to note that exports exclude archived projects.
Note that the cache is not removed.
pass: Write a note that explains the change.

name: Opener that announces

source.quote: Openers that announce. "In today's fast-paced digital world."

message: This opener says nothing the reader came for.
fix: Delete it and start with the point.

flag: In today's fast-paced digital world, teams need visibility.
pass: Teams need visibility into overdue tasks.

name: "It's not just X, it's Y"

source.quote: "It's not just X, it's Y." Say what it is.

message: The contrast frame is a machine-written tell. Say what the thing is.
fix: Delete the "not just" half and state the point.

flag: It's not just a task list, it's a workspace.
pass: A workspace holds your tasks and projects.

name: Moreover, Furthermore, Additionally

source.quote: Moreover, Furthermore, and Additionally chaining paragraphs together.

message: These connectors stitch paragraphs together without adding a fact. Each paragraph should stand on its own first sentence.
fix: Delete the connector. If the paragraphs need a link, make it a fact.

flag: Moreover, the connector retries failed requests.

name: Stacked hedges

source.quote: Stacked hedges. "It's generally usually best to typically avoid." One hedge that states a real limit can stay.

message: Two hedges in a row cancel each other and leave the reader with no fact. One hedge that states a real limit can stay.
fix: Use only the one hedge that is true, or state the condition.

flag: It's generally usually best to typically avoid this.
pass: Avoid this unless the project is archived.

name: Thanks, celebration, and apology in release notes

source.quote: Keep thanks, celebration, and apology out of the entries. They belong in the announcement, if anywhere.

message: Release note entries state what changed. Thanks, celebration, and apology belong in the announcement, if anywhere.
fix: Start the entry with what changed, from the reader's side.

flag: We're excited to announce that exports now include archived projects.

name: Entry starts with a ticket or pull request

source.quote: Start each entry with what changed, from the reader's side. Not the ticket number, the team, or the pull request.

message: The reader cares about the change, not the ticket.
fix: Lead with the change: "Exports now include archived projects." Put the ticket at the end if you need it.

flag: - PROJ-1234: Exports now include archived projects.

name: Use fictional data in examples

source.quote: Mark placeholders so nobody copies them into production: <your-api-key>, example.com, user@example.com. Never paste a real key, token, password, internal hostname, or customer record.

message: An email address that isn't on an example domain could be a real person's. Screenshots and samples use fictional data.
fix: Use user@example.com or another reserved example domain.

flag: Send the invite to jane.doe@somecompany.com.

name: Looks like a real key or token

source.section: Editing someone else's text > Edit or flag
source.quote: Something that looks like a real key, password, or customer record in a sample: Flag, replace it with a placeholder.

message: A long mixed string of letters and digits in prose looks like a key or token. Even an expired one shouldn't be published.
fix: Replace it with a placeholder such as <your-api-key>.

flag: Use the key sk9f8a7sd6f5g4h3j2k1l0z9x8c7v6b5n4m3 in the header.
pass: Use the key <your-api-key> in the header.

name: No all caps for emphasis

source.quote: No all caps for emphasis. In UI, a short badge (PREVIEW, BETA, NEW) is the one exception.

message: Capitals read as shouting and screen readers may spell them out. A short UI badge is the one exception.
fix: Use normal case. If the sentence needs weight, give it its own short sentence.

flag: NEVER restart the service during a deployment.
pass: Don't restart the service during a deployment.

name: No internal capitals unless the brand uses them

source.quote: No internal capitals unless the brand uses them. GitHub keeps its capital H. A generic report builder isn't ReportBuilder.

message: A generic feature or term doesn't take internal capitals. A brand that styles its name that way keeps it, and a code identifier belongs in code style.
fix: Write it as two lowercase words, or put an identifier in code style.

flag: Open the ReportBuilder to start.
pass: Open the report builder to start.

name: Lowercase the spelled-out form of an acronym

source.quote: Lowercase the spelled-out form unless it's a proper noun: single sign-on (SSO), role-based access control (RBAC).

message: The acronym is in capitals, but its expansion is ordinary words. Only a proper noun keeps capitals.
fix: Write "single sign-on (SSO)". Use capitals only for a product or company name.

flag: Turn on Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).

name: Acronym used without an expansion

source.quote: Spell out on first use. Write the term, then the acronym in parentheses. Skip the expansion for acronyms every reader knows, such as USB, FAQ, URL, and PDF.

message: This acronym appears without an expansion anywhere in the document. Readers who don't know it have nowhere to look. Acronyms every reader knows are skipped, and a product code or a defined term may be a false positive.
fix: Write the term, then the acronym in parentheses, the first time it appears. If the term is used only once, spell it out and drop the acronym. Inside parentheses, write only the term.

flag: Turn on SCIM before you invite people.
pass: Turn on cross-domain identity management (SCIM) before you invite people. SCIM runs hourly.
Each file has a SHA-256 hash, and every delivery is signed with HMAC under the MIT License, from a folder on your PATH.

name: Don't skip heading levels

source.quote: Don't skip levels. A third-level heading sits under a second-level heading, not directly under the title.

message: This heading is more than one level deeper than the heading before it. Readers and screen readers lose the outline.
fix: Promote the heading, or add the missing level.

source.quote: One top-level heading per page: the title.

message: The page already has a top-level heading. A second one makes two titles.
fix: Make this a second-level heading.

name: Don't stack two headings

source.quote: Don't stack two headings with no text between them. If you're editing, flag it rather than inventing text.

message: This heading follows another heading with no text between them. The reader gets two labels and no content.
fix: Flag it for the author. Either add a sentence under the first heading or remove one of them.

source.quote: Two to seven items. If you're editing a longer list, don't cut items. Split it under subheadings, or flag it.

message: This list has more than seven items. Long lists are hard to scan. Don't cut items if you're editing.
fix: Split the list under subheadings, or flag it for the author.

name: Never leave a table cell blank

source.quote: Never leave a cell blank to mean "nothing here." Write None or Not applicable. If you're editing and don't know which, flag it.

message: A blank cell could mean none, not applicable, or forgotten.
fix: Write "None" or "Not applicable". If you don't know which, flag it.

fix: End the sentence with a period.

name: Same link twice in one section

source.quote: Don't link the same destination more than once in a section.

message: This section already links to the same destination.
fix: Link only the first mention, and make the rest plain text.

source.quote: Menu paths: Bold labels joined by a spaced greater-than sign, which isn't bold. Select Settings > Members > Invite.

message: Menu paths join bold labels with a plain, spaced greater-than sign that is not itself bold. Arrows and other separators are flagged.
